places.name: Temple of Philae (Agilkia Island)
places.ai_summary: An ancient temple complex dedicated to the goddess Isis, relocated to Agilkia Island to save it from flooding.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the early morning or late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Take a boat ride to the island and enjoy the scenic views.

places.name: Unfinished Obelisk
places.ai_summary: A massive obelisk abandoned in the quarry due to cracks, offering insights into ancient stone-cutting techniques.

opening_hours.notes: Bring water and sun protection as the site is exposed.

places.place_tip: Explore the quarry to see other smaller artifacts.

places.name: Aswan High Dam
places.ai_summary: A modern engineering marvel that controls the flow of the Nile River, creating Lake Nasser and providing hydroelectric power.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the late afternoon for sunset views.

places.place_tip: Visit the nearby Lake Nasser viewpoint for stunning photos.

attribution.title: Abusimbel
attribution.author: "Per-Olow" - Per-Olow Anderson (1921-1989)
attribution.credit: sv:Forskning & Framsteg 1967 issue 3, page 16
attribution.description: Ramses's face to the "number two" colossal statue is lifted into place, since the great temple is built on the above-lying plateau. Face weighs 19.6 tonnes and concrete reinforcement in the back of 4.58 tons. Between corners, the distance 108 cm. The temple's facade is 33 meters high and 38 m wide. The temple is hewn from the rock.

places.name: Nubian Museum
places.ai_summary: A museum showcasing the history, art, and culture of Nubia, with artifacts salvaged from the Nile's floods.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Tuesdays.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the reconstructed tomb and the mummified remains.
